source_text: Hoc etiam Apostoli confirmat auctoritas, cum enim beatus Paulus de mortuorum resurrectione loqueretur, ait: Insipiens, tu quod seminas non vivificatur 51, et infra: Deus autem dat illi corpus prout vult, et unicuique seminum proprium corpus 52. Si ergo Deus humano semini, quod nemo negat vel prudentium vel piorum proprium sicut omnibus rebus corpus attribuit, unde quemquam reum natum probabis? Tandem oro respicias, quibus laqueis peccati naturalis suffocetur adsertio. Verum age tecum, precor, mitius. Mihi crede, etiam te Deus fecit, sed, quod fatendum est, gravis error infecit. Quid enim potest profanius dici, quam quod Deus hominem aut non fecerit aut, ut dicis, diabolo fecerit, aut certe diabolus Dei sit imaginem, hoc est hominem fabricatus, quod non minus stultum dinoscitur esse quam impium? Ergo tam inops tam inverecundus Deus est, ut non habuerit quod in praemium sanctis hominibus daret, nisi quod deceptis diabolus infudit in vitio? Vis autem scire, quod etiam in his, qui sancti non sunt, hanc generationum potentiam Deus tribuisse probetur? Eo igitur tempore, cum Abraham metu percussus gentis barbarae Sarram, quae uxor erat, sororem suam dixit, refertur Abimelech rex illius provinciae adduxisse eam in noctis usum. Sed Deus, cui curae erat honor sanctae mulieris, in somnis Abimelech veniens regiam frenavit audaciam comminatus interitum, si pergeret violare coniugium. Tunc Abimelech ait: Numquid, Domine, gentem ignorantem et iustam perdes? Nonne ipsi dixerunt se germanitate coniunctos? Surrexit ergo mane Abimelech et accepit mille didragma argenti et oves et vitulos et pueros et ancillas et dedit Abrahae atque a se mulierem remisit intactam. Oravit vero Deum Abraham pro Abimelech; et sanavit Deus Abimelech et uxorem et ancillas eius Deus orante Abraham curavit potentia dispensationis secretae, quae amota est verecundis vilium feminarum, quia clauserat Deus aforis omnem vulvam in domo Abimelech 54. Vide ergo utrum naturaliter malum dici debet, quod interdum aufert exasperatus Deus redditque placatus. Ipse facit et piorum filios et impiorum, quoniam quod fiunt parentes, ad naturam pertinet, quae Deo gaudet auctore; quod autem impii sunt, ad studiorum pravitatem, quae unicuique de libera voluntate contingit
pass_a_gloss: This also the Apostle's authority confirms, for when blessed Paul was speaking of the resurrection of the dead, he says: Fool, what you sow is not made alive; and below: But God gives it a body as he wills, and to each of the seeds its own body. If therefore God attributes to human seed its own body as to all things — which no one of the prudent or of the godly denies — whence will you prove anyone born guilty? I pray that you at last look back at the snares in which the assertion of natural sin is strangled. But come, I pray, more mildly with yourself. Believe me, God made you too, but, what must be confessed, a heavy error has infected you. For what can be said more profane than that God either did not make the human being, or, as you say, made him for the devil, or certainly that the devil fashioned God's image, that is the human being, which is discerned to be no less foolish than ungodly? Is God therefore so poor, so shameless, that he did not have what to give holy human beings as a reward, except what the devil poured into the deceived as a vice? He himself makes both the sons of the godly and of the ungodly, since that they become parents belongs to nature, which rejoices in God as author; but that they are ungodly belongs to the wickedness of pursuits, which comes to each from free will. God, Abraham praying, healed by the power of a hidden dispensation what was removed from the modest parts of the lowly women, because God had closed every womb from outside in the house of Abimelech. See therefore whether that ought to be called evil by nature which God sometimes, exasperated, takes away and, appeased, gives back.

pass_b_english: [Noah and his sons] were blessed in the same way as Adam and Eve, when God said: “Increase and multiply, fill the earth, and rule over it” (Genesis 9:1; Genesis 1:28) (1 Corinthians 15:36).

Therefore this pleasure, which you wish to make appear diabolical, was already present in the couples mentioned above. Good in its institution, it also continued under the blessing. There is no doubt that “Increase and multiply and fill the earth” (1 Corinthians 15:38) was said to Noah and his sons about the union of bodies whose practice had already become established (Genesis 1:26–27) (Genesis 20:18).

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
